questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni orúkọ tí à ń pè àwọn ìró tí a ń pè láìsí ìdènà afẹ́fẹ́ nínú ẹnu, gẹ́gẹ́ bí 'a', 'e', 'i'?
questions.explanation: Vowels (fáwẹ́lì) are speech sounds produced without any obstruction to the airflow, unlike consonants.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni orúkọ tí à ń pè àwọn ìró tí a ń dá pẹ̀lú ìdènà afẹ́fẹ́ ní apá kan ẹnu, gẹ́gẹ́ bí 'b', 'k', 'd'?
questions.explanation: Consonants (kọ́nṣónántì) are produced by obstructing the airflow at some point in the vocal tract, distinguishing them from vowels.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Fáwẹ́lì Yorùbá tí a ń pè pẹ̀lú afẹ́fẹ́ tí ń jáde láti imú ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Nasal vowels (àfofún) are produced with airflow passing through the nose, distinct from oral vowels (àránmú) which use only the mouth.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Fáwẹ́lì Yorùbá tí a ń pè pẹ̀lú afẹ́fẹ́ tí ń jáde láti ẹnu nìkan ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Oral vowels (àránmú) are produced with air passing only through the mouth, as opposed to nasal vowels which involve nasal airflow.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni orúkọ tí à ń pè ètò lẹ́tà tí a ń fi kọ èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Àkópọ̀ lẹ́tà refers to the standard Yoruba alphabet and orthographic system used to write the language.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ nínú èdè Yorùbá níbi tí a ti ń yọ fáwẹ́lì kan kúrò nígbà tí ọ̀rọ̀ méjì bá pàdé, láti mú ọ̀rọ̀ sunwọ̀n?
questions.explanation: Vowel elision (ìsúnkì fàwẹ́lì) occurs when a vowel is dropped where two words meet, smoothing the pronunciation of connected speech.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó ń mú kí fáwẹ́lì kan yí padà láti bá fáwẹ́lì tó wà nítòsí rẹ̀ mu, ní èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Vowel assimilation (ìyọpọ̀ fáwẹ́lì) occurs when a vowel changes to become more similar to a neighbouring vowel, aiding smoother pronunciation.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Èdè Yorùbá ní irú àmì ohùn mélòó?
options: Mẹ́ta: Òkè, Àárín, àti Ìsàlẹ̀ (three: High, Mid, and Low)
questions.explanation: Yoruba has three tone levels: high (òkè), mid (àárín, typically unmarked in writing), and low (ìsàlẹ̀), each capable of distinguishing word meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Àmì wo ni a máa ń lò láti fi hàn pé ọ̀rọ̀ kan ní ohùn òkè ní èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: A high tone in written Yoruba is typically marked with an acute accent (´) placed above the relevant vowel.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Àmì wo ni a máa ń lò láti fi hàn pé ọ̀rọ̀ kan ní ohùn ìsàlẹ̀ ní èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: A low tone in written Yoruba is typically marked with a grave accent (`) placed above the relevant vowel.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ohùn Àárín (mid tone) ní èdè Yorùbá, ní ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà, ni a máa ń kọ
questions.explanation: The mid tone in Yoruba is conventionally left unmarked in writing, distinguishing it from the marked high and low tones.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí nìdí tí àmì ohùn (tone marking) fi ṣe pàtàkì gan-an nínú kíkọ èdè Yorùbá?
options: Nítorí kò ní ipa kankan lórí ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀
Nítorí ọ̀rọ̀ kan náà lè ní ìtumọ̀ tó yàtọ̀ pátápátá tí ohùn rẹ̀ bá yàtọ̀
Nítorí àwọn olùkọ́ nìkan ló ń lò ó
Nítorí kò sí ìyàtọ̀ láàrin ohùn
questions.explanation: Since Yoruba is a tonal language, the same sequence of letters can carry entirely different meanings depending on the tone applied, making accurate tone marking essential.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ìpín kan tó kéré jùlọ nínú ọ̀rọ̀ tó ní fáwẹ́lì nínú, tí í ṣe ìpìlẹ̀ fún kíkọ ọ̀rọ̀?
questions.explanation: A syllable (ìpín-ọ̀rọ̀) is the basic phonetic unit built around a vowel, forming the foundational building block of spoken words.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ẹ̀ka ìmọ̀ èdè wo ni ó ń kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ nípa ètò ìró àti ohùn nínú èdè kan?
questions.explanation: Phonology is the branch of linguistics dedicated to studying the sound system of a language, including vowels, consonants, and tone patterns.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ẹ̀ka ìmọ̀ èdè wo ni ó ń kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ nípa bí a ṣe ń pe ìró pẹ̀lú ẹ̀yà ara ìpè (articulatory features)?
questions.explanation: Phonetics studies the physical articulation of speech sounds, complementing phonology's focus on the sound patterns and system of a language.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kọ́nṣónántì méjì tí a ń pè papọ̀ ní àkókò kan náà, gẹ́gẹ́ bí 'gb' àti 'kp', ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Labial-velar consonants like 'gb' and 'kp' are produced with a simultaneous double articulation, a distinctive feature of Yoruba phonology.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìpín-ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó parí pẹ̀lú fáwẹ́lì, ní èdè Yorùbá?
options: Ìpín-ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ṣí sílẹ̀ (open syllable)
questions.explanation: An open syllable ends in a vowel sound, a very common syllable structure in Yoruba words.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ohun tí ó ń ṣẹlẹ̀ nígbà tí ọ̀rọ̀ méjì bá pàdé tí wọ́n sì di ọ̀rọ̀ kan ṣoṣo nínú ọ̀rọ̀ sísọ àti kíkọ?
questions.explanation: Contraction in Yoruba often occurs when two words merge into one form during speech, closely related to processes like vowel elision.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ìyàtọ̀ láàrin ohùn Òkè àti Ìsàlẹ̀ nínú ọ̀rọ̀ kan náà lè yí ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ padà pátápátá. Èyí fi hàn pé Yorùbá jẹ́
options: èdè tí a kò lè kọ sílẹ̀
èdè tí kò ní ohùn rárá
questions.explanation: Because tone alone can distinguish meaning, Yoruba is classified as a tonal language, where pitch is a core part of word meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìwádìí nípa bí ohùn (tone) ṣe ń ṣiṣẹ́ nínú ìṣètò ìró èdè kan?
questions.explanation: Tonology, a specialised branch of phonology, focuses on how pitch patterns (tones) function to convey meaning within a tonal language.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ọ̀rọ̀ Yorùbá, ìró kọ́nṣónántì méjì tí a ń pè pẹ̀lú fífọwọ́kan ètè méjèèjì ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Bilabial consonants, such as 'b', 'p', and 'm', are produced using both lips, a common consonant category in Yoruba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí nìdí tí ìmọ̀ ìpín-ọ̀rọ̀ (syllable structure) fi ṣe pàtàkì nínú kíkọ́ ọ̀mọ̀wé láti ka èdè Yorùbá dáadáa?
options: Nítorí ó jẹ mọ́ orin nìkan
Nítorí ó ń ràn wá lọ́wọ́ láti mọ bí a ṣe ń pín ọ̀rọ̀ sí ẹ̀ka kéékèèké fún kíkà tí ó tọ́
Nítorí ó jẹ mọ́ ìtàn Yorùbá nìkan
questions.explanation: Understanding syllable structure helps learners correctly break down and pronounce words, supporting accurate reading and speech.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ọ̀nà tí a ń gbà ṣàyẹ̀wò ipò ahọ́n nínú ẹnu nígbà tí a bá ń pe fáwẹ́lì kan pàtó?
questions.explanation: Analysing tongue position during vowel articulation helps distinguish different vowel qualities within a language's phonological system.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ìdí tí àkópọ̀ lẹ́tà (orthography) fi ṣe pàtàkì nínú kíkọ èdè Yorùbá lónìí?
options: Kí a lè ní ìṣọ̀kan ní bí a ṣe ń kọ àti kíka èdè náà láàrin gbogbo àwọn tí ń lò ó
Kí a lè yẹra fún kíkọ èdè náà pátápátá
Kí a lè yí èdè náà padà pátápátá
Kí a lè dá kọ́nṣónántì tuntun sílẹ̀ láìsí ìlànà
questions.explanation: A standardised orthography ensures consistency in how the language is written and read across all its users, aiding clear communication and education.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìró tí a ń pè pẹ̀lú fífi ahọ́n kan ẹ̀yìn ẹnu, gẹ́gẹ́ bí 'k', 'g', 'ng'?
questions.explanation: Velar consonants, such as 'k', 'g', and 'ng', are articulated with the back of the tongue raised toward the soft palate (velum).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń dárúkọ ènìyàn, ibi, tàbí ohun kan ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: A noun (ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ) is the part of speech used to name a person, place, or thing.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń rọ́pò orúkọ nínú gbólóhùn, bí í ṣe 'òun', 'wọ́n', 'àwa'?
questions.explanation: A pronoun (ọ̀rọ̀-arọpò-orúkọ) stands in place of a noun, such as 'he/she/it' (òun), 'they' (wọ́n), or 'we' (àwa).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń fi hàn ìṣe tàbí ipò kan nínú gbólóhùn, bí í ṣe 'lọ', 'jẹ', 'jókòó'?
questions.explanation: A verb (ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe) expresses an action or state, forming the core of the predicate in a Yoruba sentence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń ṣàpèjúwe orúkọ kan, bí í ṣe 'dára', 'dúdú', 'ńlá'?
questions.explanation: An adjective (ọ̀rọ̀-àpèjúwe) describes or modifies a noun, providing more information about its quality.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń so orúkọ tàbí arọ́pò-orúkọ pọ̀ mọ́ apá gbólóhùn mìíràn, bí í ṣe 'ní', 'lórí', 'sí'?
questions.explanation: A preposition (ọ̀rọ̀-atọ́kùn) links a noun or pronoun to another part of the sentence, indicating relationships such as location or direction.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ọ̀nà tí a ń gbà kọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ tuntun nípa fífi ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ kún ìpìlẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ kan, ní èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Prefixation (àfòmọ́-ìbẹ̀rẹ̀) is a word-formation process in Yoruba where a prefix is attached to a root, often creating a noun from a verb.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ọ̀nà tí a ń gbà tún ọ̀rọ̀ ṣe lẹ́ẹ̀mejì tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ láti fi kún ìtumọ̀ rẹ̀, ní èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Reduplication (àpòpò-ọ̀rọ̀) involves repeating a word or part of it, a common word-formation process used to intensify or extend meaning in Yoruba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni gbólóhùn tí a ń pè ní 'gbólóhùn oníbọ̀' (complex sentence)?
options: Gbólóhùn tí ó ní ọ̀rọ̀ kan ṣoṣo
Gbólóhùn tí ó ní ìpín méjì tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ tí wọ́n so pọ̀ láti fi hàn èrò kan tó pé
questions.explanation: A complex sentence (gbólóhùn oníbọ̀) combines two or more clauses, often joined by a conjunction or subordinator, to express a fuller, more elaborate idea.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni gbólóhùn tí a ń pè ní 'gbólóhùn alákòópọ̀' (compound sentence)?
options: Gbólóhùn tí ó ní ọ̀rọ̀ kan ṣoṣo
Gbólóhùn tí ó ní gbólóhùn olómìnira méjì tí a fi ọ̀rọ̀ atapọ̀ so pọ̀
questions.explanation: A compound sentence (gbólóhùn alákòópọ̀) joins two independent clauses together, typically using a conjunction such as 'àti' (and) or 'ṣùgbọ́n' (but).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtúpalẹ̀ gbólóhùn, kí ni à ń pè apá tí ó ń fi hàn ẹni tàbí ohun tí gbólóhùn ń sọ̀rọ̀ nípa rẹ̀?
questions.explanation: The subject (kókó-ọ̀rọ̀) identifies who or what the sentence is primarily about, typically performing the action of the verb.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtúpalẹ̀ gbólóhùn, kí ni à ń pè apá tí ó ń fún wa ní ìsọfúnni nípa kókó-ọ̀rọ̀?
questions.explanation: The predicate (àsọtúnsọ) provides information about the subject, typically including the verb and any related objects or complements.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ìdí ìtúmọ̀ (translation) fi ṣe pàtàkì láàrin èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sì àti Yorùbá?
options: Kí a lè yẹra fún kíkọ gbólóhùn
Kí a lè fi ọ̀rọ̀ kan náà kọ ní èdè kan náà lẹ́ẹ̀mejì
Kí a lè yí ohùn ọ̀rọ̀ padà nìkan
Kí a lè fi ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ hàn ní èdè mìíràn láìyẹ̀ nínú ìtumọ̀ àti àṣà náà
questions.explanation: Translation aims to accurately convey the meaning of a passage from one language to another, while preserving both meaning and cultural nuance.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ẹ̀ka gírámà wo ni ó ń kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ nípa ìgbékalẹ̀ inú ọ̀rọ̀, gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìpìlẹ̀ àti àfikún rẹ̀?
questions.explanation: Morphology studies the internal structure of words, including how roots, prefixes, and reduplication combine to form new words.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ẹ̀ka gírámà wo ni ó ń kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ nípa bí a ṣe ń to àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ jọ láti kọ́ gbólóhùn tó ní ìtumọ̀?
questions.explanation: Syntax examines how words are arranged and combined to form grammatically correct and meaningful sentences.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń so ọ̀rọ̀ méjì tàbí gbólóhùn méjì pọ̀, bí í ṣe 'àti', 'ṣùgbọ́n', 'tàbí'?
questions.explanation: A conjunction (ọ̀rọ̀-atapọ̀) joins words, phrases, or clauses together, such as 'and' (àti), 'but' (ṣùgbọ́n), or 'or' (tàbí).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú gbólóhùn Yorùbá, kí ni orúkọ tí a ń fún ẹni tí ó ń gba ìṣe ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe, tí kì í ṣe kókó-ọ̀rọ̀?
questions.explanation: The object of a sentence receives the action of the verb, distinct from the subject, which performs the action.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè gbólóhùn tí a ń fi béèrè ìbéèrè, bí í ṣe 'Ṣé o lọ sí ilé-ìwé?'
questions.explanation: An interrogative sentence is used to ask a question, distinct from declarative, imperative, or exclamatory sentence types.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè gbólóhùn tí a ń fi pàṣẹ tàbí kọ́ni, bí í ṣe 'Lọ sí ilé-ìwé!'?
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command or instruction, such as telling someone to go to school.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀-àpèjúwe tí ó ń fi ìṣàkóso ẹnìkan hàn, bí í ṣe 'mi', 'rẹ', 'wọn' nínú 'ilé mi', ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Possessive determiners like 'mi' (my), 'rẹ' (your), or 'wọn' (their) show ownership or association with the noun they modify, such as 'ilé mi' (my house).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìfiwéra tí a ń ṣe láàrin nǹkan méjì nípa lílo ọ̀rọ̀ bí í ṣe 'ju... lọ' ní èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Comparative constructions, such as those using 'ju...lọ' (more than), allow speakers to compare the qualities of two things in Yoruba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìdìpọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń fi ìní ọ̀rọ̀ kan hàn lórí òmíràn, bí í ṣe 'ilé bàbá mi'?
questions.explanation: A possessive (genitive) construction, such as 'ilé bàbá mi' (my father's house), shows a relationship of ownership between two nouns.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtúpalẹ̀ gbólóhùn, kí ni à ń pè ìpín gbólóhùn kan sí àwọn ẹ̀yà rẹ̀ láti ṣàyẹ̀wò ìgbékalẹ̀ rẹ̀?
questions.explanation: Sentence parsing involves breaking a sentence into its grammatical components to analyse its structure and function.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ọ̀rọ̀ tí a fi ń ṣàpèjúwe ìye tàbí iye nǹkan, bí í ṣe 'mẹ́ta', 'púpọ̀', 'díẹ̀'?
questions.explanation: Quantifiers and numerals, such as 'mẹ́ta' (three), 'púpọ̀' (many), or 'díẹ̀' (a few), express quantity or amount in relation to a noun.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ìlànà gbogbogbòò tí a ń tẹ̀lé nígbà tí a bá ń kọ́ ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ láti inú ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe nípa àfòmọ́-ìbẹ̀rẹ̀?
options: Yíyí ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe padà sí kọ́nṣónántì nìkan
Fífi fáwẹ́lì kún ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe náà, bí í ṣe 'kọ́' di 'ìkọ́'
Kíkọ ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe náà ní ìdàkejì rẹ̀
questions.explanation: A common Yoruba word-formation pattern involves adding a vowel prefix to a verb root to derive a related noun, such as 'kọ́' (to build) becoming 'ìkọ́' (building/construction).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe tí ó ń fi hàn pé ìṣe kan ṣẹlẹ̀ ní àkókò tí ó ti kọjá ni a ń pè ní ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe onígbà
questions.explanation: Past tense verb forms indicate that an action has already occurred, marked in Yoruba typically through auxiliary markers or context.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè lẹ́tà tí a fi ń kọ sí ilé-iṣẹ́ tàbí ẹnì kan tí a kò mọ̀ dáadáa, ní ọ̀nà oníṣẹ́ẹ́?
questions.explanation: A formal letter is written to an institution or person one does not know well, following a professional, structured format.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè lẹ́tà tí a fi ń kọ sí ọ̀rẹ́ tàbí ẹbí, ní ọ̀nà ìbáṣepọ̀?
questions.explanation: An informal letter is written to a friend or family member in a warm, familiar tone, distinct from the professional style of a formal letter.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè àpilẹ̀kọ tí ó ń jíyàn fún tàbí lòdì sí kókó kan pẹ̀lú ìdí tó fẹsẹ̀múlẹ̀?
questions.explanation: An argumentative essay (àbáye/àjírò) presents reasoned arguments to support or oppose a particular viewpoint on a topic.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè àpilẹ̀kọ tí ó ń ṣàlàyé ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ kan tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ gan-an, ní ọ̀nà ìròyìn?
questions.explanation: News report writing (ìròyìn) describes real events in a factual, structured manner, typical of journalistic composition.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè àpilẹ̀kọ tí ó ń sọ ìtàn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ kan, pẹ̀lú ìbẹ̀rẹ̀, àárín, àti òpin?
questions.explanation: A narrative essay (ìtàn) tells the story of events, typically organised with a beginning, middle, and end.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Iye ọ̀rọ̀ tí a ń retí nínú àrokò WAEC ní èdè Yorùbá jẹ́ kò kéré ní
questions.explanation: WAEC Yoruba compositions are typically expected to contain a minimum of about 300 words to adequately develop the topic.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè kíkàwé tí a ṣe láti fa kókó pàtàkì jáde nínú àpilẹ̀kọ tí a kò tíì rí rí?
questions.explanation: Comprehension (àkàgbóòye) involves carefully reading an unseen passage to extract main ideas and understand its deeper meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú àkàgbóòye, kí ni à ń pè ìdámọ̀ àwọn kókó tí ó fara sin nínú àpilẹ̀kọ, tí kò fi hàn gbangba?
questions.explanation: Identifying implicit meaning requires the reader to infer ideas that are suggested by a text but not directly and explicitly stated.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìdámọ̀ àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ àtijọ́ tàbí ìṣàkàwé ọ̀rọ̀ nínú àkàgbóòye?
options: Kíka ọjọ́ tí a tẹ ìwé jáde nìkan
questions.explanation: Identifying idiomatic or archaic phrasing helps the reader decode figurative or older expressions whose meaning may not be obvious from a literal reading.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ìṣísẹ̀ àkọ́kọ́ tí ó yẹ kí akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ gbé ṣáájú kí ó tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí kọ àrokò?
options: Ṣíṣe ìtòlẹ́sẹẹsẹ èrò àti ìjìnlẹ̀ òye kókó náà
questions.explanation: Before writing an essay, it is important to plan and organise one's thoughts, ensuring a clear understanding of the topic to produce a coherent composition.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú lẹ́tà oníṣẹ́ẹ́, kí ni ó yẹ kí a kọ ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ìwé, ṣáájú orúkọ ẹni tí a ń kọ sí?
options: Àdírẹ́sì ẹni tí ó kọ ìwé àti ọjọ́ tí a kọ ìwé náà
questions.explanation: A formal letter conventionally begins with the sender's address and the date, before the recipient's details and the letter's body.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtàn, kí ni à ń pè apá tí ó ń parí gbogbo ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó ti ṣẹlẹ̀ nínú ìtàn náà?
questions.explanation: The conclusion (òpin) resolves the events and conflicts developed throughout the narrative, bringing the story to a satisfying end.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú àpilẹ̀kọ àbáye, kí ni ó yẹ kí òǹkọ̀wé ṣe láti fún ìdí rẹ̀ lókun?
options: Fífúnni ní ìdí àti àpẹẹrẹ tí ó ń fi ìdí èrò rẹ̀ múlẹ̀
Kíkọ gbólóhùn tí kò bára mu pẹ̀lú kókó náà
Yíyẹra fún fífúnni ní ìdí kankan
questions.explanation: An effective argumentative essay provides supporting evidence and relevant examples to reinforce the writer's position on a topic.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìtúpalẹ̀ tí a ń ṣe láti mọ ìdí tí òǹkọ̀wé fi kọ ìwé kan?
questions.explanation: Analysing the author's intention involves considering the purpose behind a text and the message the writer aims to convey.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú àkàgbóòye, kí ni à ń pè kókó pàtàkì tí ìwé kan gbé kalẹ̀?
options: Ọjọ́ tí a tẹ ìwé jáde nìkan
questions.explanation: The main idea or theme of a passage represents its central focus, the primary point the text seeks to communicate to the reader.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ó yẹ akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ṣe lẹ́yìn tí ó parí kíkọ àrokò rẹ̀, kí ó tó fi lé olùkọ́ lọ́wọ́?
options: Ṣíṣàyẹ̀wò rẹ̀ padà láti tọ́ àwọn àṣìṣe gírámà àti àkọtọ́ sí
Fífi lé olùkọ́ lọ́wọ́ láìṣàyẹ̀wò padà
questions.explanation: Reviewing one's work before submission helps identify and correct grammatical errors and spelling mistakes, improving overall composition quality.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí a ń lò láti so èrò pọ̀ ní ọ̀nà tí ó bára mu nínú àrokò, bí í ṣe 'ní àkọ́kọ́', 'lẹ́yìn náà', 'níkẹyìn'?
questions.explanation: Connecting words like 'ní àkọ́kọ́' (first), 'lẹ́yìn náà' (then), and 'níkẹyìn' (finally) help organise ideas logically within a composition.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú lẹ́tà àjọṣepọ̀, kí ni ìkíni tí ó bára mu jùlọ láti bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìwé sí ọ̀rẹ́?
options: Ìkíni onínú-adùn, bí í ṣe 'Ọ̀rẹ́ mi ọ̀wọ́n,'
questions.explanation: Informal letters to friends typically open with warm, familiar greetings, distinct from the formal openings used in official correspondence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú àpilẹ̀kọ àpèjúwe, kí ni ó yẹ kí òǹkọ̀wé ṣe láti mú kí ohun tí ó ń ṣàpèjúwe hàn kedere sí òǹkàwé?
options: Lílo ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó ń fi hàn àwọ̀, ìró, àti bí ohun kan ti rí lára
questions.explanation: Effective descriptive writing uses vivid sensory details, such as colours, sounds, and physical sensations, to bring a scene or subject to life for the reader.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìròyìn, kí ni ó yẹ kí òǹkọ̀wé rí i dájú pé ó jẹ́ nípa ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí a ń ròyìn?
options: Òtítọ́ àti pé ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní tòótọ́
Àròsọ tí kò sí ní tòótọ́
questions.explanation: News reports should be based on factual, verifiable events, distinguishing them from fictional narrative writing.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ààtò ìdálórúkọ ọmọ tuntun, ní àṣà Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: The naming ceremony (ìsọmọlórúkọ) is a traditional Yoruba rite performed to formally give a name to a newborn baby.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ètò ìgbéyàwó ní àṣà Yorùbá, láti ìbéèrè títí dé ìgbéyàwó gan-an?
questions.explanation: Ìgbéyàwó refers to the traditional Yoruba marriage process, including courtship customs and the wedding itself.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ààtò ìdálẹ̀kú àti sísin òkú ní àṣà Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Ìsìnkú describes the traditional Yoruba customs surrounding death, mourning, and burial.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìbọ̀wọ̀ àti ìkíni tí a ń fi hàn sí àgbà ní àṣà Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Ìbọ́wọ̀ fún àgbà reflects the deep cultural value placed on respecting and honouring elders, expressed through specific greetings and conduct.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ẹ̀sìn ìbílẹ̀ tí ó gbàgbọ́ nínú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ Òrìṣà àti ètò ìṣàyẹ̀wò Ifá?
questions.explanation: Traditional Yoruba religion (ẹ̀sìn ìbílẹ̀) centres on the worship of various Orisa deities and consultation with the Ifa divination system.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ètò ìṣèlú ìbílẹ̀ Yorùbá, kí ni orúkọ oyè tí ó ń tọ́ka sí ọba kan?
questions.explanation: Oba is the traditional title for a Yoruba king, the paramount ruler of a kingdom or town in the traditional political hierarchy.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ètò ìṣèlú ìbílẹ̀ Yorùbá, kí ni orúkọ oyè tí ó ń tọ́ka sí olórí abúlé tàbí ìlú kékeré tí kìí ṣe ìjọba Oba?
questions.explanation: Baálẹ̀ refers to the head of a smaller settlement or community that does not hold full kingship status.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ìgbìmọ̀ àwọn ọlọ́lá ìlú tí ó ń ràn Oba lọ́wọ́ láti ṣàkóso ìlú, tí ó sì lè ṣàyẹ̀wò agbára rẹ̀?
questions.explanation: The Ọ̀yọ́mèsì was a council of chiefs in the traditional Oyo Yoruba political system, holding significant power to check and, in extreme cases, remove the Alaafin.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ẹgbẹ́ àṣírí tí ó ní ipa pàtàkì nínú ìṣèlú àti ìdájọ́ ìbílẹ̀ láàrin àwọn ìlú Yorùbá kan?
questions.explanation: The Ogboni society is a traditional secretive fraternity that historically played a significant judicial and political role in some Yoruba communities.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni orúkọ sáà-níṣẹ́ ìbílẹ̀ tí ó ń kàn iṣẹ́ agbéṣin irin, gẹ́gẹ́ bí ọ̀nà ìgbẹ́mìí àwọn Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Alágbède refers to the traditional occupation of blacksmithing, a valued craft in Yoruba society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni orúkọ sáà-níṣẹ́ ìbílẹ̀ tí ó ń kàn iṣẹ́ àgbẹ̀, ọ̀kan lára àwọn iṣẹ́ ìpìlẹ̀ ìbílẹ̀ Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Àgbẹ̀ refers to farming, one of the most fundamental traditional occupations among the Yoruba people.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni orúkọ sáà-níṣẹ́ ìbílẹ̀ tí ó ń kàn iṣẹ́ ìrọ aṣọ, gẹ́gẹ́ bí ọ̀nà iṣẹ́ ọwọ́ Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Adárosùn refers to the traditional craft of fabric dyeing, notably associated with indigo (aro) dyeing in Yoruba culture.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni eré ìdárayá ìbílẹ̀ tí a ń fi ìjà ara-ẹni ṣe láàrin ọ̀dọ́mọkùnrin méjì, títí tí ẹnìkan yóò fi ṣubú?
questions.explanation: Ìjakadi is a traditional wrestling sport where opponents grapple until one is thrown down, a popular form of Yoruba traditional entertainment.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni eré ìbílẹ̀ tí a ń fi àwọn ìjì kéékèèké àti ihò ṣeré, tí a mọ̀ sí eré ọpọ́n?
questions.explanation: Ayò ọlọ́pọ́n is a traditional Yoruba board game played with seeds moved between carved pits, a popular form of intellectual entertainment.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ọ̀rọ̀ kúkúrú tí ó kún fún ọgbọ́n, tí a ń lò láti fi hàn ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà rere ní ọ̀nà kúkúrú?
questions.explanation: Proverbs (òwe) are short, wisdom-laden sayings used to convey deep meaning or moral lessons concisely in Yoruba speech.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè lílo ọ̀rọ̀ tàbí àpèjúwe tí kì í ṣe ìtumọ̀ tààrà, láti fi ṣàpèjúwe ohun kan ní ọ̀nà arékérekè?
questions.explanation: Figures of speech (àpèjúwe/àpóló) use language creatively, beyond its literal meaning, often for comparison or emphasis.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè eré ìbéèrè arọ́wọ́tó tí ó ń jẹ́ kí àwọn èèyàn wá ìdáhùn rẹ̀, ní àṣà Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Riddles (àwòko/àlọ́) are traditional oral puzzles designed for entertainment and to sharpen listeners' wit.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè oríkì tàbí ewì tí a ń kọ láti ẹnu, gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìjálá tàbí Ekun Iyawo, láìsí kíkọ sílẹ̀ ní àkọ́kọ́?
questions.explanation: Chanted oral poetry, such as Ijala (hunters' chants) and Ekun Iyawo (bridal lament), forms a rich tradition of performed verse within Yoruba oral literature.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìwé tí a kọ sílẹ̀ ní ìrísí ìtàn àròsọ, eré ìtàgé, tàbí ewì tí a kọ sílẹ̀, ní èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Written literature (lítírẹ́ṣọ̀ olórí-ìwé) refers to literary works recorded in text form, such as novels, plays, and written poetry anthologies.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtúpalẹ̀ lítírẹ́ṣọ̀, kí ni à ń pè kókó pàtàkì tí ìwé kan gbé kalẹ̀ láti ẹnu sí ẹnu?
questions.explanation: The theme of a literary work is the central message or idea that the author conveys throughout the text.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtúpalẹ̀ lítírẹ́ṣọ̀, kí ni à ń pè ẹni tí ó wà nínú ìtàn, pẹ̀lú ìwà rẹ̀ àti ipa tí ó kó nínú ìtàn náà?
questions.explanation: A character is a person portrayed within a literary work, defined by their traits, actions, and role in the story.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtúpalẹ̀ lítírẹ́ṣọ̀, kí ni à ń pè ibi àti àkókò tí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ inú ìtàn kan wáyé?
questions.explanation: Setting refers to the time and place in which a story's events unfold.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè iṣẹ́ ìbílẹ̀ tí ó jẹ mọ́ ìtọ́jú ẹran-ọ̀sìn àti oko ní àṣà Yorùbá?
options: Ọ̀gbìn àti Ẹran ọ̀sìn (agriculture and animal husbandry)
questions.explanation: Agriculture and animal husbandry have traditionally formed an important part of the Yoruba economy, alongside crafts like weaving and dyeing.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ètò ìjọba ìbílẹ̀ ti ìlú Yorùbá kan (bí Ọ̀yọ́) ń pè ìgbìmọ̀ tí ń ràn Oba lọ́wọ́ nínú ìdájọ́ àti ìṣèlú, tí ó yàtọ̀ sí Ọ̀yọ́mèsì?
questions.explanation: Alongside the Ọ̀yọ́mèsì, the Ogboni society traditionally served an important, sometimes overlapping, judicial and political function in some Yoruba towns.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí nìdí tí ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́ àṣà (culture) fi ṣe pàtàkì gẹ́gẹ́ bí apá kan nínú ìkẹ́kọ̀ọ́ èdè Yorùbá?
options: Kí àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ lè kọ ìṣirò
Kí àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ lè gbàgbé àṣà ìbílẹ̀ wọn
Kí àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ lè kọ èdè mìíràn tí kò jẹ mọ́ Yorùbá
Kí àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ lè lóye ìṣe àti ìrònú àwọn ará Yorùbá pọ̀ mọ́ èdè wọn
questions.explanation: Studying culture alongside language helps students understand the social practices and worldview of the Yoruba people, deepening their linguistic competence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìtàn àròsọ tí a ń kọ láti ẹnu sí ẹnu, tí ó jẹ́ kún fún ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà rere ní àṣà Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Folktales are traditional oral stories, often conveying moral lessons, passed down through generations among the Yoruba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìlànà tí a ń tẹ̀lé láti ṣàyẹ̀wò ìwé lítírẹ́ṣọ̀ kan fún kókó-ọ̀rọ̀ àti ọgbọ́n inú rẹ̀?
questions.explanation: Literary analysis involves closely examining a text's themes, characters, and structure to deepen understanding of the author's work.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni ipa tí àwọn baba ńlá (ancestors) kó nínú ìgbàgbọ́ ẹ̀sìn ìbílẹ̀ Yorùbá?
options: Wọn kò ní ipa kankan nínú ìgbàgbọ́ ìbílẹ̀
A gbà pé wọ́n ń bójútó ìdílé wọn láti ayé mìíràn, a sì ń bọ̀wọ̀ fún wọn
questions.explanation: Ancestral reverence forms an important part of traditional Yoruba belief, with ancestors regarded as continuing to watch over and guide their families.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè oríkì tí a ń kọ fún ọmọ ọba tàbí ìdílé pàtàkì kan, gẹ́gẹ́ bí ara oríkì ìbílẹ̀ Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Oríkì (praise poetry) celebrates the qualities, lineage, and achievements of an individual or family, a significant form of Yoruba oral literature.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni à ń pè ìpìlẹ̀ ìṣàkóso ìbílẹ̀ Yorùbá tí ó gbé ọ̀wọ̀ àti ipò lélẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí a ti ń jogún oyè láti ìran dé ìran?
questions.explanation: Traditional Yoruba political structures are often built around hereditary chieftaincy, with royal titles and positions passed down through specific lineages.
